# S378 — Grok: classify the usage-limit error as out

*Proposed.* The grok classifier maps the usage-limit text to the out class, so ork marks grok out for `VendorOutFor` and the role falls back to its next row, as for codex out of credits.

**Findings:** 2026-11-16 20:21: two runs with grok as first implementer (S179 run ork-20261116-200151-55ff, S359 run ork-20261116-202144-c7bb) stopped with "implementer round 1 exited unclassified" and made no edit. A headless write call reproduced it (orchestrator probe, `.scratch/grok-probe2/`, grok 1.0.77): exit 1, stderr "Error: You've reached your free Grok Build usage limit for now. Get SuperGrok for much higher limits, or try again later: https://grok.com/supergrok?referrer=grok-build", and a stream `result` with `subtype` `error_during_execution` and the same text in `errors`. The classifier knows only "used all available credits" (`internal/agent/grok/grok.go:40-42,297`). · **Size:** S · **Tree:**

## Why

*Proposed.* An unclassified exit stops the run for the owner (`internal/engine/ledger.go:45-46`); a usage limit is a vendor-out case that needs no owner decision.
